analysis: Docs-only PR: docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md (head, lines 94-171 new 'Supervised App Attest worker candidate' section) and docs/consumer/verification.md (patch adds paragraph after line 23). No code or enforcement changes are included, so no direct regression. The docs describe a default-off Stage D design: a child of the same Developer ID-signed executable makes DeviceCheck calls. The parent keeps the X25519 endpoint private key (A-003). The parent and child authenticate via LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit token, CodeDirectory identity and full SHA-256 checks. Typed RPC only (no sign(hash)); retire-before-replace. It explicitly states no extra trust, no lifetime extension, no fallback Apple call in the parent, and that it is not production-qualified. Relevant IDs: A-003, A-015, A-016, TB-002, TB-011, T-053, T-056, T-057. Claims are consistent with the existing assumptions: coordinator-side authorization, final-handoff rechecks and the endpoint binding are unchanged. Coverage limit: the worker implementation files cited (Worker/*.swift, ProviderLoop+AppAttestWorker.swift) are not supplied, so claims such as parent-only key custody, peer authentication and kill/reap semantics were not verified against code. A later code PR should be reviewed against these claims, including the new local IPC surface, the local-process impersonation risk, and the worker-slot DoS/quarantine behavior. The threat model may later need a TB-011 or TB-003 note on the worker IPC boundary once the feature is enabled. Documentation drift: the code-map table and the 'Related' links are unchanged. The Mermaid chart on lines 109-119 is plain text.
